witness: Unnamed observers, reported by Maria Joaquina Tavares de Proença de Almeida Garrett
excerpt_pt: Sabe V. Revᵃ, que aqui na Granja houveram pessoas que viram o movimento de rotação do sol e a nuvem côr de rosa passar por diante do sol?
summary_en: Writing the next day, Garrett says people at Granja saw apparent solar rotation and a pink cloud pass in front of the Sun. She herself had attended the Cova; this is her report about other observers.
source: DCF III-1, document 79, pp. 214–215. Manuscript reference: AForm, Doss. 3, fl. 4, doc. 2. Printed Portuguese pages visually checked.
recorded_direction: No compass direction or viewing angle recorded.
limitations: Observers are unnamed. No exact observation point, clock time, or bearing. Contemporary evidence of a report at a remote location, not a triangulation measurement.

witness: Unnamed local observers, reported by Adelaide Grego
excerpt_pt: aqui em Torres Novas á mesma hora tambem se manesfestou no sol qualquer cousa, mas pela discripção que me fazem não se pode cumparar...
summary_en: Grego says something also appeared in the Sun at Torres Novas at the same hour, but the descriptions given to her were not comparable to what she had seen at Fátima.
source: DCF III-1, document 319, p. 740. Manuscript reference: AForm, Doss. 6, fl. 52, doc. 11. Printed Portuguese page visually checked.
recorded_direction: No compass direction or viewing angle recorded.
limitations: Grego was at Fátima; this passage relays local reports. Brief and explicitly less dramatic than the Cova account.

witness: Painter José Leite, reported by daughter Berta Leite through Maria do Carmo Lopes da Fonseca
summary_en: Berta reports that her father, painting coastal rocks, stopped because the Sun appeared to turn and returned home delighted. She explicitly says she did not accompany him that day.
source: Diogo Pacheco de Amorim, University of Coimbra mathematician, O Instituto 122 (1960), p. 197, §128. Quotes Fonseca’s letter dated 17 August 1958, forwarding Berta’s account. Portuguese page visually checked.
recorded_direction: No direction toward Fátima or angular measurement recorded.
limitations: A daughter’s later account of her father’s experience, transmitted through correspondence; not her own eyewitness report. Parede is where they were staying, not a second independent sighting.

witness: Afonso Lopes Vieira, with wife Helena de Aboim Lopes Vieira and mother-in-law
record_date: Later account; Portuguese publication checked: 1960 and edition with 1966 imprimatur
summary_en: Portuguese sources preserve the poet’s account of an unfamiliar brilliant spectacle viewed from his veranda, plus a report that his wife and others joined him. Haffert records his widow’s confirmation in 1960.
source: João de Marchi, Era uma Senhora mais brilhante que o Sol, p. 176 (PDF p. 181; this edition has a 1966 imprimatur). Amorim (1960), p. 196, §126, citing Costa Brochado, pp. 315–316. Haffert (1961), p. 40.
recorded_direction: Portuguese passages retrieved give no measured bearing. Haffert’s English narration places the spectacle over the mountain at Fátima.
limitations: Town marker approximates the known house’s locality; not a surveyed viewing station. Do not transform the narrator’s identification with the Cova event into a measured eastward azimuth.

witness: Inácio Lourenço, schoolchildren, teacher Delfina Pereira Lopes and villagers
record_date: Later letter, date not established from the retrieved passage
summary_en: Lourenço describes leaving school after cries outside, a pale rotating disc, apparent zigzag descent, fear, and colors on surrounding people and objects. De Marchi says he questioned the teacher and other villagers to corroborate the account.
source: João de Marchi, Portuguese edition, pp. 176–177 (PDF pp. 181–182). Amorim (1960), pp. 176 and 202–203. Portuguese passages retrieved; De Marchi source text and relevant page images saved.
recorded_direction: Account identifies the Sun but supplies no compass bearing or angular measurement.
limitations: Exact 1917 school position not established. Plotted at the settlement. Haffert’s English retelling attributes the school narrative to Joaquim; the Portuguese material distinguishes the brothers and groups.

witness: Joaquim Lourenço, mother and approximately twenty people on a nearby hill
record_date: Recorded by Fonseca in letter dated 1958-06-10; recollection of conversation the previous year
summary_en: Fonseca reports Joaquim’s account of a group waiting on a hill with a wide view of the Fátima ridges, followed by apparent rotation, three descents, colored light and panic. Fonseca remembers local alarm but says she does not remember seeing the phenomenon herself.
source: Diogo Pacheco de Amorim, O Instituto 122 (1960), appendix pp. 202–204; Fonseca letter dated 10 June 1958. Portuguese pages visually checked.
recorded_direction: The hill offered a view of Fátima’s ridges. This is not an explicit measured bearing to the observed disc.
limitations: Hill is unidentified. Same locality marker as the school; two groups are distinguished in the source but must not be treated as fully independent records of every detail. Prior expectation of a celestial sign is explicitly described.

witness: Albano Barros, tending sheep near Minde
summary_en: In Haffert’s published interview, Barros recalls a falling Sun in the direction of Fátima while tending sheep. He says he was too distracted to remember other details.
source: John M. Haffert, Meet the Witnesses (1961), pp. 40–41 (PDF pp. 62–63). Author’s published interview retrieved in English. Portuguese edition Encontro de Testemunhas is catalogued but its text/original interview record was not located in this pass.
recorded_direction: English published interview explicitly says “in the direction of Fatima”; this is not a numeric azimuth.
limitations: Haffert says a village near Minde, not an exact field. Town marker is approximate; the bearing to Cova is a calculation, not a measurement reported by Barros. Portuguese wording remains unverified.

witness: Guilhermina Lopes da Silva and two workmen
summary_en: In Haffert’s published interview, Silva says that, unable to attend Fátima, she looked toward the mountain at noon, saw a great red flash and called two workmen who also saw it.
source: John M. Haffert, Meet the Witnesses (1961), pp. 41–42 (PDF pp. 63–64). English interview retrieved. A separate early claim of observers in Leiria is quoted by Amorim, appendix p. 202, from O Mensageiro dated 8 November 1917; newspaper issue not retrieved.
recorded_direction: English says toward the mountain; neither the peak nor a compass bearing is specified.
limitations: The published address is where she was living around 1960; the passage does not establish it as her 1917 observation address. Town marker only. Muse dates the early newspaper passage to 5 November; Amorim says 8 November. Portuguese interview text remains unverified.
